key_insight: A knowledge-guided neural network interatomic potential can achieve reliable reactive-energy predictions for energetic materials with far fewer training configurations by combining enriched basis functions, adaptive sampling, and key-event selection.
engineering_relevance: This approach lowers the data burden for building transferable machine-learning potentials that can support safer, faster prediction of pyrolysis, isomerization, and shock-response behavior in energetic materials.
method: Enhanced NNAP with sphmulti: extra radial basis plus element-specific chemical weighting in each radial channel.
Used hyperactive learning, farthest-point sampling, and iterative sufficiency criteria to retain important configurations.
Guided training with key events relevant to reactive pathways in 3,3'-diamino-4,4'-azoxyfurazan.
evidence_signal: The model was trained on only 13,680 configurations and reproduced the isomerization barrier, pyrolysis activation energy, and shock Hugoniot behavior.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful selection of key events and sampling strategy, so transferring the workflow to other energetic systems could require re-tuning.
paper_title: Knowledge-Guided Construction of Machine Learning Potentials for Reactive Behavior in Energetic Materials
